title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 548-550): Grothendieck compares two homomorphisms defined on a 'tilde' extension of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,oo}. He has the lifted extension T~_{1,1} -> GL(2, Z^) and wants to identify it with the 'modular' fundamental homomorphism of the theory of elliptic curves, Gamma_Q -> pi_1(M_{1,1,Q}) -> GL_2(Z^). On the previous page he observes that the two agree on mu_2(Z^) = {+-1}^P.

Top of this page: it follows that the two homomorphisms differ by a homomorphism Pi^{ab}_{0,3,Q} -> mu_2(Z^) = {+-1}^P. He reduces this to a homomorphism
G_m(Z^)_2 = (Z^*)_2 = {+-1}^P -> _2G_m(Z^) = mu_2(Z^),
so that the arithmetic (cyclotomic) part is what matters. He notes such a map is determined by a few values (the reading of 'un carré' is uncertain). He states that the two probably coincide, but that he has not tried to prove it.

Second part: the formulas (35), (36) concern the arithmetic correction terms Theta_rho, Theta_sigma. These are attached to the symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,oo} of order 2 and 3, whose fixed points are lambda = 1/2 (orbit {1/2, 2, -1}) and lambda = -j, -j-bar (j a primitive cube root of unity). He interprets them as the Galois action on the Tate modules of the CM elliptic curves at these points: j-invariant 1728 (CM by Z[i]) and j-invariant 0 (CM by Z[(1+sqrt(-3))/2]). He uses the Legendre identification M_{0,3,Q} = M_{1,1}[2]'_Q, the coarse level-2 moduli scheme (the lambda-line).

The sign indeterminacy in (35), (36) corresponds to lifting a rational point of the coarse space M_{1,1}[2]' to the stack M_{1,1}[2]. That stack is a mu_2-gerbe over M_{0,3}, because -1 acts trivially on 2-torsion. Concretely, the lift amounts to choosing an elliptic curve with Legendre level-2 rigidification realising the quadruple (0, 1, oo, q), with q = 1/2 or q = -j-bar. Different choices are quadratic twists, which change the Tate-module representation by a quadratic character: exactly a sign ambiguity.

The next page concludes that loop-group (GT-type) computations, 'if one had looked for them', reproduce crucial arithmetic-geometric facts: the CM Galois representations at j = 0 and j = 1728.
errors: If (Z^*)_2 denotes Z^*/(Z^*)^2, then at p = 2 the factor Z_2^*/squares is (Z/2)^2, so the identification with {+-1}^P is only abstract, not canonical. If it denotes 2-torsion, then both sides equal mu_2(Z^) and the notation is merely redundant.
The coincidence of the two homomorphisms is left as a plausibility claim without proof, as Grothendieck himself says ('je n'ai pas essayé de le prouver').

ideas.what: M_{0,3} as coarse space of level-2 (Legendre) moduli; M_{1,1}[2] is a mu_2-gerbe over it, so lifting rational points involves a sign/quadratic-twist choice.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family; X(2) minus cusps; mu_2-gerbe / quadratic twist ambiguity
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Jacobi); stack viewpoint: Deligne-Rapoport, standard
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions M_{1,1} and M_{0,4} in the Teichmüller tower; this precise statement: unsure

ideas.what: The symmetry fixed points 1/2 and -j of P^1-{0,1,oo} are the CM points j = 1728 and j = 0. The arithmetic correction terms in the 2- and 3-cycle relations for the Galois/GT action are interpreted as Galois action on Tate modules of CM elliptic curves.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on pi_1 at special (CM) base points; 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT; Hecke characters of Q(i) and Q(sqrt(-3))
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT relations: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; elliptic/M_{1,1} extensions: Nakamura-Schneps, Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps (1990s); CM link via Fermat curves and Jacobi sums: Anderson, Ihara-Kaneko-Yukinari, Coleman

ideas.what: Comparing the lift T~_{1,1} -> GL(2,Z^) with the modular representation pi_1(M_{1,1,Q}) -> GL_2(Z^); agreement up to a character into mu_2(Z^).
ideas.modern_name: Extension of the GT/Galois action to the profinite modular group SL_2(Z)^ and Gamma_{1,1}

missed.claim: Conjecture that the two homomorphisms (the one from the M_{0,3}~ / T~_{1,1} construction and the modular one) coincide exactly, not just modulo a character Pi^{ab} -> mu_2(Z^). This is unproved here.
missed.quote: C'est vraisemblable[ment] que les deux coïncident — je n'ai pas essayé de le prouver
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a precise compatibility statement between the GT-style action on genus-0 data and the genus-1 modular Galois representation, with an explicit possible defect in {+-1}^P. It could be checked against the Nakamura-Schneps and Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps descriptions of GT acting on Gamma_{1,1}.

missed.claim: The sign ambiguities in the explicit 2-cycle and 3-cycle correction terms (fixed points 1/2 and -j) are exactly the quadratic-twist ambiguities in choosing a CM elliptic curve (j = 1728, j = 0) with Legendre level-2 structure. Loop-group computations would thus recover the CM Galois characters.
missed.quote: ils doivent correspondre simplement à l'action de Γ_Q sur les modules de Tate des courbes elliptiques à multiplications exceptionnelles, correspondant justement aux pts (1/2, 2, -1) et (-j, -j̄)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The CM/Jacobi-sum content of Galois action on pi_1(P^1-{0,1,oo}) is known via Fermat quotients (Anderson, Ihara). Interpreting the GT 2- and 3-cycle relation terms specifically via CM Tate modules at j = 1728 and j = 0, with signs explained by the mu_2-gerbe M_{1,1}[2] -> M_{0,3}, is a concrete framing I am not sure appears explicitly in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page links the arithmetic correction terms at the order-2 and order-3 symmetry points of P^1-{0,1,oo} to CM Galois representations at j = 1728 and j = 0, with sign ambiguities explained by the level-2 gerbe. This is a natural and correct insight, and partially reflected in later work (Ihara, Anderson, Nakamura-Schneps). It is a nice unpublished detail but not a startling unknown result.
transcription_corrections: 'C'est vraisemblablement sans que les deux coïncident' should probably read 'C'est vraisemblable[ment] que les deux coïncident'.
'caractérisé par ses valeurs [?] int. [?] qui est un carré' is largely illegible. It plausibly concerns values on specific elements and whether -1 is a square; uncertain.
Here j denotes a primitive cube root of unity, so the points -j, -j̄ are e^{±iπ/3} (j-invariant 0), and the points 1/2, 2, -1 give j-invariant 1728.
'la quadruple [?] (0,1,∞,q)': likely 'la quadruple (0,1,∞,q)', the four branch points of the Legendre double cover.
